issues.was: `!/.claude/audits/` re-admitted the whole audits directory, weakening the whitelist guarantee the rest of the .gitignore block relies on.
checked: ORACLE CHOICE. I did not rely on the bare check-ignore exit code, per your warning. The oracle was `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, which lists exactly the paths that are untracked AND not ignored — it cannot be fooled by a negation match.
ARM 1 (verdict trackable): the four AUDIT-*.json files under .claude/audits/*/ are the ONLY entries it returns.

ARM 2 (stray ignored): I created .claude/audits/effort-websearch-1-19-4/stray-probe.txt and it did not appear. Also probed one level deeper — .claude/audits/effort-websearch-1-19-4/sub/AUDIT-nested.json — and it did not appear either, so the `*/` glob binds to a single level as intended and a nested tree cannot smuggle files in. Both probes removed afterwards; `git status` is clean.

THE GIT CLAIM IS ITSELF CORRECT, and I verified it rather than accepting it. On an untracked file matching the negation, `git check-ignore -v` prints `!/.claude/audits/*/AUDIT-*.json` and exits 0; on a genuinely ignored stray in the same directory it prints `/.claude/audits/**` and also exits 0. Both cases exit 0, so the exit code cannot discriminate — the CHANGELOG's caveat and the choice of `git status` as the oracle are both right.

The file already routes mechanism independence explicitly onto the two unconfounded flag rows, so nothing downstream leans on row 6's mechanism column. Note also that env's precedence is separately demonstrated elsewhere, over agent frontmatter (ctl-fmenvhigh: a delegate declaring `effort: high` still ran xhigh, which settings-only pinning would not produce, since fm-high proves frontmatter otherwise wins).
